blocks.text: The **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** split one state into two on **2 June 2014** — residual AP keeping ~58% of population and ~55% of territory (13 districts then; 26 after 2022's re-districting) but losing the capital, its revenue engine and institutional depth. Analyse implications on a **six-domain grid** — administrative, economic, social, political, cultural, legal — each with its transitional wound and its adaptive response.

rows: **Administrative**

Capital-less statehood (Secretariat operating from Hyderabad's 10-year window, Sec 5 — then Velagapudi interim); **cadre division chaos** (IAS/IPS allocations contested; Sec 77-80 employee division dragging years); records, institutions, training academies all Telangana-side
Interim Secretariat (2016-); new directorates built from scratch; the secretariat-village system (2019) as a leapfrog — adversity midwifing innovation
**Economic**

~45% revenue loss with 58% population (services-IT receipts Hyderabad-locked); revenue deficit from day one; debt-share disputes (population-ratio division of ~₹97,000 crore public debt; asset division asymmetric — fixed assets by location favoured Telangana's Hyderabad endowment)
Sunrise-state strategy: ports-corridors-aqua; EoDB rank-1 positioning; central packages pursued (the RMA-013 scorecard)
**Social**

Families-jobs-education networks split; students' fee-reimbursement and admissions transition (common admissions till 2024 window under Sec 95); health-referral dependence on Hyderabad's corporate hospitals
AIIMS Mangalagiri & new institution buildout; 371D continuation protecting existing allocations
**Political**

Seat shrink (LS 25, Assembly 175) → reduced Delhi weight; party system reset (regional bipolarity; the SCS-betrayal narrative as the dominant cleavage 2014-19); Rayalaseema's renewed periphery anxiety (capital moved coastward again)
Special-status politics; the 2018 NDA exit & 2024 coalition pivot — AP's leverage politics
**Cultural**

Telugu identity's split-screen (two states claiming the language's patrimony — official language bodies, film industry's Hyderabad base, festivals' 'ownership'); Hyderabad's shared-heritage wistfulness
AP's identity rebuild: Lepakshi-Amaravati heritage branding, separate academies, the 'Andhra' cultural re-centering
**Legal**

The Act's disputed provisions (next notes' subjects): Sec 46 finance, Secs 85-89 water boards, Schedule IX/X institution division (**Sheela Bhide committee** pending items), Sec 8 (Governor's Hyderabad law-order role, lapsed 2024)
Litigation + negotiation track; SC petitions on the Act's 'arbitrary provisions' (HCOA-073's core)

sections.heading: Reading the grid — three cross-cutting judgments

items: **Asymmetric endowment, symmetric pride**: Telangana inherited the metropolis; AP inherited the coastline — the decade since is a natural experiment in **city-capital vs port-geography** development models; a mature answer scores both states' gains without grievance-mongering.

**Transition costs are governance costs**: employee allocation (years of Kamalanathan-committee wrangling), institution-splitting and records division consumed a decade of administrative energy — the case for **codified reorganisation protocols** (a standing Reorganisation Commission template) in future state-splits.

**The federal lesson set**: consent (Assembly's voice vs Art 3), compensation (statute vs assurance — RMA-013), and **continuity machinery** (who arbitrates the leftovers?) — AP 2014 is now THE case study Indian federalism teaches itself with.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'Telangana inherited the metropolis; AP inherited the coastline' — the one-line frame that organises every implication and signals balance. The Sheela Bhide & Kamalanathan committee names mark you as a details candidate.

prelimsPointers: **Appointed day: 2 June 2014**; residual AP ~58% population, 13 districts (26 from 2022).
**Sec 5**: Hyderabad as **common capital up to 10 years** (window closed 2 June 2024); **Sec 8** gave the Governor special Hyderabad law-order responsibility for that period.
**Public debt divided broadly by population ratio (~58:42)**; located fixed assets went by situs — the asymmetry grievance.
**Kamalanathan Committee** — state-cadre employee division; **Sheela Bhide Committee** — Schedule IX/X institutions' division (many items unresolved).
**Sec 95 & Schedule provisions** protected common admissions/education access for a transition window (10 years).
Residual AP's LS seats: **25**; Assembly: **175** (Act provides for future increase to 225 post-delimitation).
**AIIMS Mangalagiri** & Schedule-13 institutions — the compensatory institutional buildout.
mainsAngles: Run the six-domain audit of bifurcation's implications for residual Andhra Pradesh.
Transition is a governance project — evaluate the cadre, records and institution-division decade after 2014.
Metropolis versus coastline — compare the development models forced on the two successor states.
What should a model State Reorganisation protocol contain? Draft it from AP's 2014 lessons.
Politics after partition — analyse how bifurcation reset AP's party system and its leverage in Delhi.

glossary.definition: The continuing legal entity (AP) after carve-out — inheriting the state's identity, debts and the Act's compensatory promises.
Hyderabad's ten-year shared-capital status under Sec 5 — expired June 2024, completing the separation.
Allocating fixed assets by physical location — the rule that concentrated Hyderabad-era assets in Telangana.
Division of all-India and state services personnel between successor states — the Kamalanathan-era administrative saga.
The Act's lists of state corporations and training-research institutions requiring division — the Sheela Bhide file.
AP's post-2014 self-branding — a coastline-led, investment-hungry rebuild narrative.

sections.heading: Losing a capital — the singular wound

blocks.text: AP is modern India's only state to **lose its capital city twice** (Madras 1953; Hyderabad 2014). Hyderabad was not merely administrative HQ: it generated the lion's share of undivided AP's **services economy, IT exports (~₹57,000+ crore then), excise-stamps-registration revenue and land value** — bifurcation therefore amputated the fiscal core (the ~45%-revenue fact) while the **ten-year common-capital window (Sec 5)** offered use without ownership. The Act's answer — **Sec 6: an expert committee for the new capital** (the Sivaramakrishnan Committee, 2014 — advised distributed development, cautioned against fertile-delta mega-city) — was overtaken by the state's choice: **Amaravati** (announced 2014-15; foundation 22 Oct 2015) via the **Land Pooling Scheme** (~**34,000 acres from ~29,000 farmers** — plots-back-plus-annuity: the world's largest voluntary pooling).

rows: Construction bill vs support

Master plans (Singapore consortium) estimated lakh-crore-scale build; **central support actual: ~₹1,500 cr (capital) + ₹2,500 cr (backward regions instalments era)** — the Act promised 'assistance' without a number (**Sec 94(3)**: funds for essential facilities): the gap grievance
The 2019-24 rupture

Three-capitals proposal (**Executive: Visakhapatnam; Legislative: Amaravati; Judicial: Kurnool** — the Sri Bagh echo) + CRDA repeal (2020); farmer litigation (annuity & development covenants); **AP HC (March 2022)** ordered Amaravati's development per pooling promises; appeal pending in SC; construction frozen five years
The 2024 revival
CRDA restored; **World Bank+ADB ~$1.6 bn (~₹15,000 cr) programme**; HUDCO lines; trunk-works retendered — Amaravati as capital re-affirmed; Polavaram-Amaravati as the twin flagship rebuild
Fiscal meaning

Capital-less decade = investment-signal costs (capital flight to Hyderabad/Bengaluru/Chennai), interim-rent economy (Velagapudi), land-value stasis for pooled farmers — 'the cost of not deciding' as a public-finance case

sections.heading: Assessment — building a capital as state-building

items: **The pooling innovation**: consent-based assembly (vs acquisition's coercion) with returnable developed plots + 10-year annuity + jobs promises — praised as win-win, critiqued for tenant-labourer exclusion (annuities reached owners; the landless got pensions) and delta-ecology concerns (Sivaramakrishnan's caution) — both sides in two sentences.

**Capital-location theory**: concentrated greenfield (Amaravati's Naya-Raipur model) vs distributed functions (three-capitals' decentralisation claim) vs organic metro (Vizag's existing base) — each has federal precedents; AP's decade tested all three rhetorically while building none fully: the governance-continuity lesson (HCOA-069's protocol argument) lands hardest here.

**The financial-implications verdict**: losing Hyderabad cost a revenue engine; the capital saga then cost a **decade of agglomeration** — the double loss; the 2024 revival with multilateral finance converts the file from grievance to project — answers should end on the build, not the bruise.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'AP lost a metropolis in 2014 and a decade to indecision after' — then pivot to the 2024 revival. The Sivaramakrishnan-vs-Amaravati tension and the tenant-exclusion critique of pooling are the depth markers.

prelimsPointers: **Sec 6, Reorganisation Act** mandated an expert committee on the new capital — the **K.C. Sivaramakrishnan Committee (2014)** favoured distributed development, flagged delta-farmland loss.
**Amaravati foundation: 22 October 2015 (Uddandarayunipalem)**; master-planning by a **Singapore consortium**; CRDA Act 2014.
**Land Pooling Scheme: ~34,000 acres, ~29,000 farmers** — returnable plots + 10-year annuity; the largest voluntary urban pooling anywhere.
**Three-capitals proposal (2020)**: Visakhapatnam (executive), Amaravati (legislative), Kurnool (judicial) — with CRDA repeal; **AP HC struck the course (3 March 2022)**, SC appeal pending.
**2024 revival**: CRDA restored; **World Bank ~$800 mn + ADB ~$800 mn (≈₹15,000 crore)**; Union budget (July 2024) anchored it.
Central capital assistance actually released in the first decade: **~₹1,500 crore** (plus backward-district grants) — against Sec 94(3)'s open-ended promise.
Interim seat: **Velagapudi Secretariat (2016)**; High Court at Amaravati (Nelapadu) from 2019.
mainsAngles: Twice orphaned of its metropolis — assess the financial meaning of Hyderabad's loss for residual AP.
Land pooling was consent's experiment — evaluate Amaravati's LPS on equity, ecology and enforceability.
Concentrated, distributed or organic — adjudicate AP's three capital models with federal precedents.
The decade of indecision cost more than the bifurcation — argue with investment-signal and agglomeration economics.
From grievance to project — appraise the 2024 multilateral-financed Amaravati revival and its risks.

glossary.definition: Voluntary land assembly returning developed plots plus annuities to owners — Amaravati's acquisition-without-eminent-domain model.
Capital Region Development Authority (2014; repealed 2020; restored 2024) — Amaravati's statutory builder.
Productivity gains from urban concentration — what a capital city seeds and a frozen capital forfeits.
The Sec-6 expert panel (2014) advising distributed capital functions and warning against fertile-delta megacity siting.
The guaranteed yearly payment to pooling farmers pending plot development — the scheme's trust instrument and litigation subject.
The 2020 decentralisation proposal (Vizag-Amaravati-Kurnool) — Sri Bagh's echo, struck down in 2022, politically retired after 2024.

sections.heading: Dividing people and firms — employees, natives, commerce

blocks.text: States can be divided by statute; **careers and markets divide slower**. The Act's people-provisions: **Secs 77-80** — services division by the **Kamalanathan Committee** (state employees allotted on options-seniority-nativity matrices; years of guidelines, objections and tribunal litigation; ~lakh-scale employees affected), **Sec 76** continuing service conditions; AIS cadres split by the Centre (the Pratyush Sinha committee exercise). The **'native issues'**: nativity certificates deciding allotment and education quotas; **Art 371D's Presidential Order re-issued for each state (2016-era adaptation)** keeping local-cadre protections alive; spouses-split-postings, Hyderabad-settled Andhra-origin employees' anxieties (opting dilemmas), and pensioners' division — the human ledger of reorganisation.

rows: Immediate shocks

Licences-permits-registrations duplicated; **excise & liquor markets split** (pricing arbitrage borders); APSRTC bifurcation (fleet/routes/debts); power-purchase agreements untangled (generation stations vs demand centres — the **Sec 92/Schedule-12 power-sharing** friction and KRMB-GRMB energy angle)
Firm-level geography

Hyderabad-headquartered firms serving Andhra markets re-registered; pharma's Vizag belt vs Hyderabad's Genome Valley — one industry, two jurisdictions; film industry (Tollywood's Hyderabad base) vs AP's audience-tax base — the entertainment-tax and ticket-pricing skirmishes as symbol
Finance & credit
Bank regional offices, SLBC restructuring; district credit plans redrawn; chit-fund/NBFC oversight split
New-border frictions → cooperation
Check-post era (2014-17) till GST (2017) dissolved fiscal borders — **GST as the accidental healer of bifurcation's trade wounds**: the one-nation-tax arriving three years after the two-state split

items: **Employee division's lessons**: options-based allotment respected agency but bred strategic gaming; nativity criteria imported identity into HR; the tribunal backlog (years of Sec-80 references) argues for **pre-announced, formula-bound, time-capped division rules** in any future reorganisation — the administrative-law takeaway.

**Commerce's lesson**: markets re-integrated faster than bureaucracies — GST, digital payments and highway logistics stitched what the Act cut; the state-border cost fell mainly on **regulated sectors** (liquor, power, transport) where government IS the market-maker: a neat political-economy observation.

**The balanced close**: ten years on, the people-division is substantially done (pensions/promotions largely settled), the firm-division absorbed — the durable residue is **institutional memory loss** (split training academies, archives) and the **Hyderabad-diaspora** of Andhra professionals whose remittance-investment behaviour now shapes both states: division's demography outlasting its paperwork.

prelimsPointers: **Secs 77-80** govern state-services division; the **Kamalanathan Committee** ran employee allotment (options-seniority-nativity).
**AIS cadre division** was overseen centrally (**Pratyush Sinha committee** exercise); Sec 76 protected service conditions.
**Art 371D Presidential Orders were adapted separately** for AP and Telangana after 2014 — local-cadre protections continue in both.
**APSRTC** was bifurcated (fleet, routes, staff, debts apportioned); power arrangements ran via **Sec 92 & Schedule 12** (existing PPAs honoured).
**Entertainment-tax/ticket and film-industry frictions** symbolised the Tollywood-in-Hyderabad vs Andhra-audience split.
**GST (1 July 2017)** ended inter-state check-post fiscal friction — three years post-bifurcation.
Pensioners and provident funds were apportioned on population/service formulas — the long-tail settlement items.
